title: Model merging: weighted, SLERP, task arithmetic

questions.q: In ModelMergeSimple, what does ratio mean?
questions.why: add_patches(k, 1 - ratio, ratio) multiplies model1 by ratio and adds model2 times 1 - ratio. Default 1.0 gives model1 unchanged.

questions.q: Two fine-tunes 8 degrees apart: how much do lerp and slerp differ?
options: By about 0.00024 per weight at most, on weights of about 0.02: hardly at all
questions.answer: By about 0.00024 per weight at most, on weights of about 0.02: hardly at all
questions.why: The two differ only when the parents are far apart. At 90 degrees, lerp's length is 0.707 of the parents'.

questions.q: What is task arithmetic at x = 0.5 and y = 0.5?
options: The same sum as a halfway lerp
questions.answer: The same sum as a halfway lerp
questions.why: base + 0.5(A - base) + 0.5(B - base) = 0.5A + 0.5B. The lab finds the difference is rounding.

questions.q: Why merge unquantized files and quantize after, by the numbers?
options: Merging quantized parents rounds again, on top of the parents' rounding: FP8's error grows from 0.026 to 0.036, and a small task vector drowns
questions.answer: Merging quantized parents rounds again, on top of the parents' rounding: FP8's error grows from 0.026 to 0.036, and a small task vector drowns
questions.why: The final file is rounded either way. Quantizing parents adds their two errors to that one. The lab's correlation with the true change falls to 0.408 at a 1% change.

questions.q: You subtract a base from a fine-tune, using FP8 files of both, and the change is 1% of the weights' size. What's read back?
options: More rounding error than change: error is about 2.2 times the change
questions.answer: More rounding error than change: error is about 2.2 times the change
questions.why: The two rounding errors don't cancel, and they're bigger than a change that small.

questions.q: Why keep your unquantized file after you quantize a copy?
options: It's your only clean source for any later merge
questions.answer: It's your only clean source for any later merge
questions.why: Rounding can't be undone, so any later merge starts from the file you kept.
